rulings.challenge_claim: The opening cut is argued as a clean speaker break while two byte-grounded lexical hooks run straight across that seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, both hooks are real and both are decision-relevant. Object one, the second-person-plural divine title: אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.9 at BYTE tier and reciprocally, and the object is distinctive rather than a generic divine name -- that word-bound form stands in only 4 verses book-wide, 2 of them the pair here (sweep: 4 verses, the 2mp-suffixed Elohim form, skeleton tier; chs 40-41 = oshb:Isa.40.1 and oshb:Isa.40.9). Its first-person-plural counterpart runs between them: לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ closes this row's own opening verse (oshb:Isa.40.3, byte tier against its own verse) and אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.8, byte tier against its own verse) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.3 at skeleton tier. Object two, the calling root, named by attested form because the plene participle is not a contiguous match for the three-letter skeleton and the skeleton sweep does not return oshb:Isa.40.3 at all (sweep: 7 verses, contiguous qr' skeleton, chs 40-41 -- oshb:Isa.40.2, 40.6, 40.26, 41.2, 41.4, 41.9, 41.25): וְקִרְא֣וּ (oshb:Isa.40.2) then קוֹרֵ֔א (oshb:Isa.40.3) then קְרָ֔א and אֶקְרָ֑א (oshb:Isa.40.6), each byte tier against its own verse. Both objects straddle both of this row's seams, and the rejected alternative rests precisely on discontinuity at web:Isa.40.2|web:Isa.40.3 while engaging neither. Under the cross-seam cohesion rule a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity unless disclosed, so the defect is real. Credit stands where OL gave it: the two single-witness SAMEKH marks at oshb:Isa.40.2 and oshb:Isa.40.5 (tier-3) verify under the claimed type, both splices are byte tier, and leaving the crier unnamed is byte-sound. Severity low is correct -- this is a disclosure gap, not an overturned cut.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add one cross-seam disclosure sentence naming both straddling objects with pointed splices and collate-true tiers -- the 2mp title אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) against oshb:Isa.40.9 at byte tier, its 1cp counterpart לֵאלֹהֵֽינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.3) / אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ (oshb:Isa.40.8) at skeleton tier, and the calling-root chain וְקִרְא֣וּ (oshb:Isa.40.2), קוֹרֵ֔א (oshb:Isa.40.3), קְרָ֔א and אֶקְרָ֑א (oshb:Isa.40.6), byte tier each against its own verse -- and state why the speaker-onset ground survives them. observed_substrate_signals: add the dotted keys for the signal classes newly consulted (divine_title.* and refrain.*), as dependent fields of the added disclosure. No respan; the cut is not challenged. TEST the cure must pass: re-collation of every added run must return exactly the tier written (the pair at oshb:Isa.40.1/oshb:Isa.40.9 must return byte and the 1cp pair must return skeleton, not byte), and a cross-seam re-check of web:Isa.40.2|web:Isa.40.3 must return no byte-true device left undisclosed -- the check that killed the original is that the seam argument stood on speaker discontinuity alone while a byte-identical title pair bracketed the row.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's principal cohesion evidence, the repeated withering-grass clause, is stated through the English with no Hebrew form and no tier, and it is not byte-recurrent.
rulings.grounds: Verified in both directions: יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֔יץ (oshb:Isa.40.7) against oshb:Isa.40.8 returns accent_stripped, and יָבֵ֥שׁ חָצִ֖יר נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֑יץ (oshb:Isa.40.8) against oshb:Isa.40.7 returns accent_stripped -- letters and vowels agree, the accents differ, so the clause is NOT byte-recurrent. The row carries this, its own load-bearing intra-unit cohesion ground, entirely in English ('the clause translated ...'), with no splice and no tier on a recurrence claim; the tier-disclosure standard requires every recurrence claim to be tier-labelled at write time, so the claim is defective as written and simultaneously understates evidence that is genuinely there at accent_stripped tier. The quote/gloss parity slip verifies too: the row's opening splice runs the whole of oshb:Isa.40.6 through כְּצִ֥יץ הַשָּׂדֶֽה while its paired curly-quoted English stops at the second question, and the WEB verse continues past that point (web:Isa.40.6). Cross-seam, the row splices אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ at its own closing verse without disclosing that this is the middle member of the byte-tier title pair אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) / oshb:Isa.40.9 that brackets the row's close. Mark handling is correct and verifies under the claimed type: SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.40.5 before the span and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.40.8 at its close (tier-3, single-witness). Severity medium is right: the defect sits on the row's principal cohesion driver, not on a decorative aside.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace the English-only refrain sentence with a spliced, tier-labelled one -- יָבֵ֤שׁ חָצִיר֙ נָ֣בֵֽל צִ֔יץ (oshb:Isa.40.7) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.8 at accent_stripped tier and reciprocally, agreeing in letters and vowels and differing in the accents, expressly NOT byte. boundary_rationale: re-cut the gloss at the opening verse so the curly-quoted WEB run and the pointed splice cover the same extent -- either carry the English through the flower-of-the-field clause (web:Isa.40.6) or trim the splice to אֶקְרָ֑א; a quote/gloss parity repair re-cuts the gloss, it does not re-cut the splice alone. device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure of the byte-tier title pair אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) / oshb:Isa.40.9 straddling this row's close. TEST the cure must pass: re-collation of the refrain pair must return accent_stripped, so any 'byte', 'verbatim' or 'byte-identical' wording fails -- that is the check that killed the original -- and a quote/gloss extent re-check at the opening verse must show the English and the pointed run ending at the same clause.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected alternative asserts a form-class fact the bytes contradict: neither an imperative nor a feminine-singular addressee carries forward into web:Isa.40.10-Isa.40.11.
rulings.grounds: The refuted sentence is the row's own strongest_rejected_alternative, which states that 'the imperative and addressee both carry forward unchanged from web:Isa.40.9'. Re-derived from the pointed bytes, the two following verses carry no imperative and no second-person form of any gender: יָב֔וֹא (oshb:Isa.40.10) under a presentative, then יִרְעֶ֔ה, יְקַבֵּ֣ץ, יִשָּׂ֑א and יְנַהֵֽל (oshb:Isa.40.11), each byte tier against its own verse, all third-masculine-singular yiqtol. The one feminine form in the pair, the participle מֹ֣שְׁלָה (oshb:Isa.40.10), agrees with the feminine arm-noun standing beside it in the same clause, and both witnesses render it of the arm and not of an addressee (web:Isa.40.10). Form-class labels are byte-checkable claims under the same discipline as digits, so this is a defect, not a reading preference. The herald address itself is byte-sound as the row has it (אַל תִּירָ֔אִי and the 2fs suffixes, oshb:Isa.40.9, byte tier). Two further arms verify: neither following verse is spliced at all, so the continuity ground is carried in English alone, and the byte-tier title pair אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) against oshb:Isa.40.9 straddles this row's opening seam undisclosed. Marks at oshb:Isa.40.8 and oshb:Isa.40.11 verify under the claimed type (SAMEKH, tier-3, single-witness). The cut is NOT overturned -- the row's other ground survives and is byte-supported by the presentative chain -- but its stated warrant is false, so medium stands.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: delete the clause asserting that the imperative and the addressee carry forward unchanged, and replace it with the byte-true continuity warrant -- the presentative particle carries the herald's commanded announcement across the verses, הִנֵּ֖ה (oshb:Isa.40.9) re-collating against oshb:Isa.40.10 at accent_stripped tier where it stands twice, הִנֵּ֨ה and הִנֵּ֤ה (oshb:Isa.40.10, byte tier against its own verse) -- keeping the one-sentence limit plus the optional mandated-rival sentence. device_notes: splice at least one form from each of oshb:Isa.40.10 and oshb:Isa.40.11 with its tier, and record that מֹ֣שְׁלָה is feminine by agreement with the arm-noun beside it rather than by any addressee, per both witnesses' renderings (web:Isa.40.10). device_notes: disclose the byte-tier title pair אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.40.1) / oshb:Isa.40.9 across the opening seam. TEST the replacement warrant must pass: it must survive the exact check that killed the original -- every form-class label in it re-checked against the pointed bytes and both witnesses' renderings, with the revised sentence containing no claim of a carried-forward imperative or of any second-person addressee in web:Isa.40.10-Isa.40.11, and every added run re-collating to the tier written.

rulings.challenge_claim: The interrogative is used as an intra-unit cohesion argument while the same word-bound interrogative continues across this row's closing seam at three further sites (sweep: 3 verses), undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Object and tier both verify. The row argues that 'the interrogative form recurs at web:Isa.40.13-Isa.40.14 as an internal chain rather than a fresh onset', i.e. it uses the interrogative as an intra-unit cohesion signal. Re-derived word-bound -- the two-letter token matched whole-token against the consonantal skeletons and never as a substring -- the same token stands in 9 verses across chs 40-41 (sweep: 9 verses: oshb:Isa.40.12, 40.13, 40.14, 40.18, 40.25, 40.26, 41.2, 41.4, 41.26). Three of those sit immediately past this row's close, and two of them are structural in the next row: וְאֶל מִ֖י opens oshb:Isa.40.18, וְאֶל מִ֥י closes oshb:Isa.40.25, and וּרְאוּ֙ מִי stands mid-verse at oshb:Isa.40.26 (byte tier each against its own verse), against מִֽי at this row's own onset (oshb:Isa.40.12, byte tier). A signal that runs on immediately past the seam cannot by itself distinguish inside from outside, and the row discloses none of it while resting the same seam on the absence of a form or addressee shift. The two secondary arms verify as well: the closing verse is argued in English only, with no pointed splice for oshb:Isa.40.17, and an MT-keyed single-witness mark annotation is hung on a WEB-prefixed coordinate at web:Isa.40.16 while the correct oshb:Isa.40.16 entry also stands. Credit where OL gave it, and I re-derived it independently: the interior mark is held as presence only, and the row's statement that the next mark does not recur until oshb:Isa.40.24 is TRUE against the single-witness layer, which carries nothing at oshb:Isa.40.17 through oshb:Isa.40.23. Severity low is correct.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: disclose that the word-bound interrogative continues past this row's close at oshb:Isa.40.18, oshb:Isa.40.25 and oshb:Isa.40.26 (sweep: 9 verses, word-bound interrogative token, chs 40-41), and name the tier-1 signal that actually distinguishes the units, since the interrogative alone does not. boundary_rationale: supply a pointed splice with its tier for the closing verse oshb:Isa.40.17, so the close is argued in the original language and not in English alone. boundary_evidence_refs: delete the entry 'web:Isa.40.16 (SAMEKH, single-witness)' -- that layer is MT-keyed and the correctly keyed oshb:Isa.40.16 entry already stands, so the WEB-prefixed one is both mis-witnessed and a duplicate. TEST the cure must pass: a span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry sweep must show every parashah annotation carried on an oshb: key only and under its claimed type; the interrogative citation must name its swept object and unit and carry a digit; and the verified-true statement that no mark falls at oshb:Isa.40.17-oshb:Isa.40.23 must survive the edit unchanged.

rulings.challenge_claim: The envelope driver is a real and exclusive object, but it is tier-labeled byte when the two verses do not recur at any tier.
rulings.grounds: The defect is real but the framing overstates it in one direction and understates the row's hedge in the other. Verified: the full runs וְאֶל מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן (oshb:Isa.40.18) against oshb:Isa.40.25 and וְאֶל מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי (oshb:Isa.40.25) against oshb:Isa.40.18 both return tier NONE, the verbs differing in the dagesh and in the first-person suffix -- so a 'tier: byte' label written over that pair is wrong. But 'do not recur at any tier' is itself byte-false: the shared two-word interrogative prefix וְאֶל מִ֖י (oshb:Isa.40.18) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.25 at accent_stripped tier. The corrected finding: the envelope is real, its recurrent portion is the interrogative prefix at accent_stripped tier and the verb pair is NOT recurrent at any tier, and the row's single joint 'tier: byte' parenthesis conflates the two while its own trailing words ('matching construction rather than an identical full clause') expressly deny identity -- an ambiguous and mislocated tier label rather than a false byte-identity assertion, which is why severity is low and not medium. OL's exclusivity digit verifies (sweep: 2 verses, contiguous liken-root skeleton, chs 40-41: oshb:Isa.40.18 and oshb:Isa.40.25; 3 verses book-wide). The remaining arms verify: the cross-seam echo at web:Isa.40.21|web:Isa.40.28 is carried with no splice and no tier (and does not recur in the Hebrew at any tier -- see this cluster's high-severity row); the closing splice carries the frame יֹאמַ֖ר קָדֽוֹשׁ (oshb:Isa.40.25, byte tier) while observed_substrate_signals names no speech-formula or divine-title key; and an MT-keyed mark is again hung on a WEB coordinate at web:Isa.40.24 beside the correct oshb: entry. The row is right not to count that bare epithet as a title site: the objects separate in the bytes (sweep: 4 verses, contiguous qadosh skeleton, chs 40-41 -- the bare epithet at oshb:Isa.40.25 against the full title at oshb:Isa.41.14, oshb:Isa.41.16 and oshb:Isa.41.20).
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: split the one joint tier label into two collate-true labels -- the shared interrogative prefix וְאֶל מִ֖י (oshb:Isa.40.18) against oshb:Isa.40.25 at accent_stripped tier, and the full runs וְאֶל מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן / וְאֶל מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי at tier NONE in both directions -- and drop 'tier: byte' from the envelope parenthesis entirely. device_notes: tier-label the cross-seam echo at web:Isa.40.21|web:Isa.40.28 or drop the recurrence framing, since it is NONE at every tier and the resemblance is a rendering fact. observed_substrate_signals: add the speech_formula.* / divine_title.* key for the frame יֹאמַ֖ר קָדֽוֹשׁ the closing splice already carries. boundary_evidence_refs: delete 'web:Isa.40.24 (SAMEKH, single-witness)', the MT-keyed layer wrongly witnessed, the correct oshb:Isa.40.24 entry standing. TEST the cure must pass: every recurrence label must equal the tier returned for the exact run quoted, so 'byte' may appear only where re-collation returns byte -- the check that killed the original -- and the mark-disclosure symmetry sweep must find no parashah annotation on a WEB key.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: a parashah division falls after this span's own opening verse at exactly the cut the row names and rejects and is not disclosed, and a cross-seam recurrence is tier-labeled byte although it does not recur in the Hebrew at any tier. LF: the row never discloses that its own opening verse carries a parashah mark, though it types every other cited mark, and the silent gap sits exactly where its rejected alternative needed it most.
rulings.grounds: The two primaries hit the SAME defect by independent routes, and it is confirmed: the single-witness mark layer carries a SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.40.26 (tier-3), a division after this span's own opening verse, which is exactly the web:Isa.40.26|web:Isa.40.27 cut the row's strongest_rejected_alternative names and dismisses on content grounds alone. The row cites oshb:Isa.40.26 bare in boundary_evidence_refs while typing oshb:Isa.40.31 as PE, so span-relevant mark symmetry is broken at the one verse in the span where the layer is decision-relevant, and it is broken in the direction that corroborates the rival being refused. Absence would never be counterevidence, but a mark present inside the span is owed. OL's three further defects are distinct and all verify. (2) The tier label is false: הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.40.21) against oshb:Isa.40.28 and הֲל֨וֹא יָדַ֜עְתָּ אִם לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ (oshb:Isa.40.28) against oshb:Isa.40.21 both return tier NONE -- second-masculine-plural imperfect against second-masculine-singular perfect, and the later verse's second question is introduced by a conditional-negative pair rather than by the interrogative particle standing four times in the earlier one. The identity is a rendering fact only: both WEB verses open “Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard?” (web:Isa.40.21, web:Isa.40.28), and the row's device_notes writes 'tier: byte' over that pair with no Hebrew quoted anywhere. (3) The closing seam is straddled undisclosed: יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֔חַ (oshb:Isa.40.31) re-collates against oshb:Isa.41.1 at accent_stripped tier and reciprocally, a catchword at the oracle join arguing continuity against the cut. (4) A paseq seg sits at oshb:Isa.40.28 (count-only, single-witness), a verse the row cites in evidence, undisclosed. Credit stands: both pointed splices are byte tier and the imperative onset שְׂאוּ מָר֨וֹם עֵינֵיכֶ֤ם (oshb:Isa.40.26, byte tier) is byte-sound. Four real defects, one of them at the decision point of the row's own rejected rival and one a false byte label on a recurrence with no Hebrew behind it: high is correct.
rulings.remedy: boundary_evidence_refs: type the mark at the span's own opening verse as 'oshb:Isa.40.26 (SAMEKH, single-witness)'. strongest_rejected_alternative: weigh that mark explicitly where the web:Isa.40.26|web:Isa.40.27 cut is refused -- name it as tier-3 single-witness corroboration standing FOR the rival, and refuse the rival on the tier-1 ground (the imperative onset supplying the evidence the complaint is answered by), never by silence; if the writer concludes the mark plus the onset shift now favour the cut, that is a boundary PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption and is not author work. device_notes: strike 'tier: byte' from the rebuke recurrence and state the collate truth -- הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.40.21) against oshb:Isa.40.28 and הֲל֨וֹא יָדַ֜עְתָּ אִם לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ (oshb:Isa.40.28) against oshb:Isa.40.21 both at tier NONE, the shared question pair being a rendering fact at web:Isa.40.21 and web:Isa.40.28. device_notes: disclose the closing-seam catchword יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֔חַ (oshb:Isa.40.31) against oshb:Isa.41.1 at accent_stripped tier. device_notes or boundary_evidence_refs: disclose the paseq at oshb:Isa.40.28 as count-only and single-witness, asserting no intra-verse position. TEST the cure must pass: a span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry sweep across oshb:Isa.40.26-oshb:Isa.40.31 must return no remainder, with each mark under its claimed type and PE never conflated with SAMEKH, and the paseq tallied; and re-collation of every recurrence run must return exactly the tier written -- the check that killed the original is that 'tier: byte' on the rebuke pair fails at every tier, so any surviving byte or verbatim wording there re-fails.

rulings.challenge_claim: OL: a single-witness Prophets parashah mark is placed in the operative position of the rejected alternative, and the span's opening seam is straddled by an undisclosed catchword. LF: the row folds a third-person craftsmen vignette into a second-person judicial summons and first-person divine self-declaration without weighing the speech-register shift between them as a candidate seam, testing only a weaker rejected alternative instead.
rulings.grounds: The two items are PARTLY the same defect and partly distinct, and one distinct arm is refuted. Same defect, reached by two routes and upheld: the row's strongest_rejected_alternative refuses the earlier close 'because the parashah SAMEKH mark closes the whole complex specifically at oshb:Isa.41.7', putting a tier-3 single-witness Prophets mark in the driving position with the content ground trailing behind an 'and'; LF states the same thing as the mark not settling whether a tier-1 frame shift sits inside that paragraph. In the Prophets that layer is corroboration only, never a boundary driver, so the sentence is defective as ordered. REFUTED, on the row's own bytes and its own text: LF's claim that the sharper register seam was 'never engag[ed]' does not hold. The register geography is that the address is second-person-plural with a first-person divine referent at oshb:Isa.41.1 (יִגְּשׁוּ֙ ... נִקְרָֽבָה, byte tier) through the self-declaration at oshb:Isa.41.4, and turns third-person at oshb:Isa.41.5 (the islands seen and afraid) and stays third-person through the craftsmen at oshb:Isa.41.6-Isa.41.7 -- so the register seams are web:Isa.41.4|web:Isa.41.5 and web:Isa.41.5|web:Isa.41.6, and the row's rejected alternative names precisely 'closing this unit at web:Isa.41.4-Isa.41.5', which is both of them. The rival LF says was never named is the rival the row tested. OL's two remaining arms are distinct and upheld: יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֑חַ (oshb:Isa.41.1) re-collates against oshb:Isa.40.31 at accent_stripped tier, a catchword straddling this row's own opening seam undisclosed; and the disclosed link to web:Isa.41.21 is carried in English with no splice and no tier although the bytes state it plainly -- יִגְּשׁוּ֙ and נִקְרָֽבָה (oshb:Isa.41.1) against קָרְב֥וּ and הַגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.41.21), byte tier each against its own verse, the same two roots in inverted order. OL's two-object count discipline verifies: the draw-near root by contiguous skeleton in chs 40-41 stands at 3 verses (oshb:Isa.41.1, 41.5, 41.21) and the bring-near root must be swept per attested spelling, the defective form at oshb:Isa.41.1 (sweep: 1 verse) against the plene at oshb:Isa.41.21 and oshb:Isa.41.22 (sweep: 2 verses), so one contiguous needle would have missed both later sites. The closing-seam texture verifies too: חֲזָֽק (oshb:Isa.41.6) against oshb:Isa.41.9 at skeleton tier through הֶחֱזַקְתִּ֨יךָ֙ (sweep: 4 verses, contiguous strengthen-root skeleton, chs 40-41). NEW FINDING, neither lens: the boundary prose co-argues from a tier-4 object, calling the onset 'a fresh chapter and unit' and the mark at oshb:Isa.40.31 as 'marking the chapter boundary'; chapter divisions are never boundary evidence. Severity medium.
rulings.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: re-order so the content ground leads -- the mutual-encouragement and idol-soldering of web:Isa.41.6-Isa.41.7 as the ironic continuation of the fear named at web:Isa.41.5 -- and demote oshb:Isa.41.7 SAMEKH to a trailing single-witness corroboration clause; keep the rival as tested, since it already names the register seam. device_notes: disclose the opening-seam catchword יַחֲלִ֣יפוּ כֹ֑חַ (oshb:Isa.41.1) against oshb:Isa.40.31 at accent_stripped tier. device_notes: splice and tier the web:Isa.41.21 summons link instead of carrying it in English -- יִגְּשׁוּ֙ and נִקְרָֽבָה (oshb:Isa.41.1) against קָרְב֥וּ and הַגִּ֨ישׁוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.41.21), byte tier each against its own verse -- counted as two named objects, the draw-near root by contiguous skeleton (sweep: 3 verses, chs 40-41) and the bring-near root per attested spelling (defective sweep: 1 verse; plene sweep: 2 verses). boundary_rationale: strike the tier-4 chapter-division co-argument ('opening a fresh chapter and unit'; 'marking the chapter boundary'), leaving the tier-1 summons formula as the driver and the tier-3 mark as corroboration. TEST the cure must pass: the revised rejected_alternative must still refuse the close at web:Isa.41.4-Isa.41.5 with the mark citation deleted from the sentence outright -- only the ground that survives that deletion may be written, which is the check that killed the original ordering; every added run must re-collate to the tier named; and no chapter-division wording may remain anywhere in the boundary prose.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two recurrence claims carrying this row's boundary weight are asserted with no Hebrew form, and the one tier-labeled byte is not byte-recurrent.
rulings.grounds: Both arms verify at the byte level. Arm one, the fear-not chain the strongest_rejected_alternative rests on: it is stated with no splice and no tier, and it is not one form -- אַל תִּירָא֙ (oshb:Isa.41.10) re-collates against אַל תִּירָ֖א (oshb:Isa.41.13) at accent_stripped tier, while אַל תִּֽירְאִי֙ (oshb:Isa.41.14) against oshb:Isa.41.13 returns tier NONE, a feminine-singular form chained with two masculine-singular ones.
